why: A story-free wrapper around window maximum with a monotonic deque: compute the maximum of every length-k window in O(n) with a decreasing deque of indices, then take the smallest of those maxima.
hints: What would you need if you knew the maximum of every window? How do you get all of them in O(n)?
Sliding window maximum: a deque of indices whose values decrease; its front is the current window's maximum.
Run the deque scan and, instead of storing the maxima, keep their running minimum. O(n) time, O(k) space.
pitfalls: k = 1: the answer is the minimum element.
k = n: the answer is the maximum element.
